title: Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Technician

8-170. MOS 170B - Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Technician (Effective 202507)
 a. Licensing/certification requirements. None.
 b. Prerequisites. . DA PAM 611-21.
 c. MOS 170B. MOS 170B is an accession MOS. The preferred CMF feeders are MOS 17E, 25E, 25S,
35N, 35S; however, all other enlisted MOSs that demonstrate a strong EW background to include
documented operational experience and education may apply. Applicants from other military services
(Air Force, Marine Corps, and Navy) who can substantiate their EW qualifications with performance
evaluations, awards, and certificates, or have ASI 1A or 1C are encouraged to apply for MOS 170B.
The proponent sets and maintains the technical qualifications for the MOS. Please refer to
https://recruiting.army.mil/ISO/AWOR/170B for current selection criteria and proponent contact
information. The Warrant Officer accessions process is available at
https://recruiting.army.mil/ISO/AWOR; please direct any accessions related questions to the Warrant
Officer Recruiting Branch at woteam@usarec.army.mil.


   d. Associated SQI.
      (1) 0--No special qualifications.
      (2) 8--Instructor.
      (3) P--Parachutist.
      (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
      (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all Warrant
Officer MOS)).
   f. Qualifications.
      (1) WO1/CW2 must--
           (a) Complete the Electromagnetic Warfare Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
           (b) Be a U.S. citizen.
           (c) Obtain a fully adjudicated TOP SECRET clearance with eligibility for access to Sensitive
Compartmented Information (SCI), prior to Warrant Officer Candidate School attendance
           (2) CW3 must--
                (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
                (b) Complete the Electromagnetic Warfare Technician Warrant Officer Advanced Course
for CW2(P) and CW3.

            (3) CW4 must--
                (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
                (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE) phase two (2)
and three (3) for CW3(P) and CW4.
            (4) CW5 must--
                (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
                (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
      (1) WO1/CW2. As an EW Technician :
          (a) Organizes, implements, monitors, and evaluates EW operations, threat environment, unit
maintenance, and intermediate level support maintenance of EW systems.
          (b) Provides advice on technical and tactical employment of all assigned EW systems and
tasked or requested non-organic EW systems to include Electromagnetic Attack (EA), Electromagnetic
Support (ES), and Electromagnetic Protection (EP) activities.
          (c) Develops, publishes, and updates EW Operations SOP incorporating current TTP.
          (d) Develops and integrates measures of performance and measures of effectiveness criteria to
determine EW battle damage assessment (BDA), re-engagement criteria, and alternate methods of
engagement.
          (e) Provides input and updates to S6 for joint restricted frequency list (JRFL) validation and
employment to include spectrum deconfliction and frequency management.
           (f) Implements spectrum interference reporting criteria and resolution tracking as received from
higher headquarters.
           (g) Recommends the use of ES for immediate target prosecution and triggering criteria and EP
measures to provide resolution.
          (h) Analyzes signal external parameters to identify a signal, correlate a threat, provide
indications and warnings, improve the Commander’s situational understanding, and to select, modify,
and/or inform the development of electromagnetic countermeasures for affecting targeted
communications and non-communications systems.
          (i) Evaluates the technical and tactical operations of subordinate EW sections.(j) Develops and
implements brigade emission control (EMCON) procedures, which includes staff coordination and SOP
change publishing.
          (k) Integrates EA, ES and EP into EW operations.
          (l) Establishes tactics techniques and procedures for operations in a contested EW
environment. In coordination with S2/S6 identify emerging EW threats or trends and develop mitigation
measures to overcome new adversarial EW actions.
          (m) Disseminates and monitors compliance with updated EW system load sets to assigned
EW entities as issued by the Cyberspace Electromagnetic Activities (CEMA) section.
          (n) Assists with technical and tactical information in order to develop and implement Appendix
12 to Annex C and associated Tabs of the Operations Order. Provide input and refinement to the S2 for
the enemy tactical EW order of battle (OB) and applicable appendices to Annex B of the operations
order.
          (o) Liaises for subordinate EW entities to higher headquarters CEMA section for EW requests
for support.
          (p) Assists with technical and tactical information in order to develop and implement the routine
EW training plan for EW system operators and staff sections involved in planning EW integration.
Perform EW training for leaders, including the command group and key staff.
          (q) Provides EW input to the intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR)
synchronization meeting, operations and intelligence (O&I) working group, and targeting/planning
meetings.
          (r) Prioritizes EW requests and operations with subordinate units and requests for support from
higher headquarters.
          (s) Serves as the key facilitator for EW and CEMA Working Groups.
          (t) Monitors and maintains EW running estimates.
          (u) Resolves EA conflicts with the S2 in intelligence gain-loss considerations.
          (v) Updates and disseminates changes to the enemy tactical EW OB to include associated
targeting information and necessary intelligence generation.
          (w)Provides technical input regarding effects requests and/or electromagnetic countermeasure
development efforts.
          (x) Develops and mentors EW Specialists.
     (2) CW3--
         (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(1).
         (b) Monitors the development of the enemy electromagnetic order of battle (EEOB) and the
processing of target information and intelligence generation.
         (c) Identifies and recommends solutions to EW capability gaps and limitations.
         (d) Acts as the Commander’s EW technical and tactical advisor.
         (e) Provides EW technical expertise to subordinate units and activities involved with EA, ES,
and EP operations to include maintenance of all EW systems activities.
         (f) Liaises between EW specialists and the theater EWC for Joint EW support.
         (g) Monitors and prioritizes the processing of EA and review EW BDA.
         (h) Coordinates for and updates applicable target selection standards and disseminates to all
subordinate EW entities.
         (i) Assists in the development and maintenance of the operational EEOB, processing of
targeting information and intelligence generation.
     (3) CW4--
         (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(2).
         (b) Recommends target purging criteria to the G3, EWC, and subordinate headquarters.
         (c) Monitors and prioritizes the processing of EA and reviews BDA at Corps level.
            (d) Synchronizes EW operations within the joint targeting cycle for Air Force, Navy, and Marine
Corps EW integration into Army operations.
           (e) Monitors the development of the enemy strategic EEOB and the processing of target
information and intelligence generation at the strategic/operational level.
           (f) Recommends the employment and directs the operation of available Theater level assets.
           (g) Assists in production and application of target selection standards at Corps level.
           (h) Requests targeting information from military intelligence and higher sources and evaluates
information obtained through the IPB process at Corps level and disseminates to assigned
organizations.
            (i) Assists in the preparation of theater Emergency Action Plans, operational plans and orders
and disseminates to assigned organizations.
            (j) Exercises EW technical supervision of strategic and operational EW operations.
            (k) Coordinates with Corps Legal section to ensure EW operations comply with law of armed
conflict and rules of engagement criteria.
      (4) CW5--
           (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g(3).
           (b) Serves as the senior technical advisor at the highest echelons of command such as HQDA,
COCOMs, ASCCs, DRUs, Joint Services and allied armies in all matters pertaining to the integration of
Electromagnetic Warfare capabilities.
           (c) Advises the US Army CY Proponent on all matters pertaining to EW Warrant Officers
professional development, career progression and Professional Military training requirements.
           (d) Liaises with CY Proponent to advise commanders on requirements for Army EW personnel
and equipment, to include training and certification.
           (e) Advises members of Theater Commands, CAOC and BCD on all matters concerning Army
EW requests, requirements, and priorities.
           (f) Develops and publishes applicable theater Request for Forces (RFF), Joint Urgent
Operational Needs Statements (JUONS), Operational Needs Statements (ONS), and Integrated Priority
Lists (IPLs) as applicable for EW requirements.
           (g) Analyzes and recommends changes to commanders on EW targeting, attack guidance,
target selection standards and coordinates EW assets to achieve strategic effects.
   h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
      (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold)
      (2) Meet medical and physical standards per AR 40-501.
          (a) Have 20/40 correctable vision per AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-13 and 5-17 and meet hearing
standards of AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-7 and 5-18.
      (3) Table 8-170B-1. Physical requirements - a minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) –
0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic
Run (IR) – 0036 shuttles.

code positions into one of four definable skill levels. W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; CW4
equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:

          (b) Table 8-170B-3, Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
